clue.text: Do them another way, as a rule

indicators.note: arranged another way tells us the letters of the two words are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Advice to tackle some tasks differently as a general habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a rule' looks like the everyday phrase meaning usually, but 'a rule' is the definition and 'as' only links it.
explanation.definitionFit: A method is a fixed procedure or system, a rule one follows.

clue.text: Grace describes quality of V. Knox's extracts

definitions.meaning: Vicesimus Knox compiled the anthology Elegant Extracts, so the quality of his extracts is in its title

explanation.surface: A note that charm is what marks a certain compiler's selections.
explanation.walkthrough: Vicesimus Knox was an 18th-century schoolmaster whose anthology was titled Elegant Extracts.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace and refinement of style are near synonyms; the anthology title supplies the second sense.

clue.text: They provide top control in hearts-possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the phrase may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Something that keeps a firm grip on the emotions, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top control' suggests mastery, but the top is the head and the control is of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Nets worn over the hair keep a hairstyle on the head in place.

clue.text: Right recipient of a playpen ?

parts.note: read play-pen as a pen for writing plays; the person who ought to be given one is a writer for the stage

explanation.surface: Who ought to be given a toddler's enclosure?
explanation.definitionFit: A playwright is the proper owner of a pen used to write plays.

clue.text: Particulars of what are not paid in cash

definitions.text: what are not paid in cash
definitions.meaning: one pays these to someone as a courtesy, not with money

explanation.surface: Details of debts that are settled some other way than with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Points of detail are 'respects'; and courtesies are 'paid' in the idiom 'pay one's respects'.

clue.text: Played the old King of Clubs at this one ?

definitions.text: Played the old King of Clubs at this one ?

parts.words: Played the old King of Clubs at this one ?
parts.note: the club is a golf club; the 'old King' is a club whose name means regal and aged, the senior club of golf, where one plays

explanation.surface: A card player wondering where they led a high club.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews, Scotland, is the historic home of golf; 'royal' is the King, 'ancient' the old.
explanation.definitionFit: The golf club's name combines a sense of kingship with great age, fitting 'old King'.

clue.text: They are by no means distinguished

definitions.text: They are by no means distinguished

parts.words: They are by no means distinguished
parts.note: read 'means' as money: people marked out by having no money at all

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about undistinguished people.
explanation.definitionFit: The destitute are people set apart by lacking any money.

clue.text: With heaven-sent talent, am rich as can be

indicators.note: the letters show what they can be when rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Someone gifted by heaven boasts of being as wealthy as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as can be' reads like an intensifier, but 'can be' marks the anagram and 'With' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word originally meant a divinely conferred gift, now personal magnetism.

clue.text: 5 ac in ghostly shape

indicators.note: put into a new shape, so the letters of that answer are rearranged

parts.note: refers to the answer to 5 across, spelt out

explanation.surface: Another entry rendered as a phantom.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5-across answer, rearranged ('in ghostly shape'), gives phantoms, which the same words describe.
explanation.definitionFit: Phantoms or apparitions are spectral shapes, ghosts.

clue.text: Proof of single-mindedness

parts.note: read 'single' as unmarried: evidence of a determination to stay unwed

explanation.surface: Evidence of focus and determination.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstaining from marriage shows a mind set on remaining unwed.

clue.text: Medicine for this clergyman about four?

definitions.text: Medicine for this clergyman about four?

parts.words: Medicine for this clergyman about four?
parts.note: a remedy word for a cleric whose charge of souls is called his cure, and who is classically served at teatime

explanation.surface: A remedy prescribed for a vicar's assistant around four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: An assistant parish priest has a 'cure' of souls; the question mark flags wordplay on that sense of medicine and teatime visits.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant to a parish priest is the junior clergyman in question.

clue.text: Though wet, it's not recorded in liquid measure

definitions.text: Though wet, it's not recorded in liquid measure

parts.words: Though wet, it's not recorded in liquid measure
parts.note: something wet that is measured in inches or millimetres of depth, not pints or litres

explanation.surface: A puzzling observation about a liquid that is measured oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipitation is gauged by depth in inches, not by volume.

clue.text: Is among those left to hold out

indicators.note: among places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the rest means the remainder, those left over
taken as written

explanation.surface: One person stays behind with the remainder to keep fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold out against something is to withstand or oppose it.

clue.text: Rare condition of dangerous ice

parts.note: rare in the sense of rarefied or sparse; dangerous ice is ice that is not thick

explanation.surface: An unusual state found in treacherous frozen water.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarity in the sense of sparseness, and the quality of ice too slight to bear weight.

clue.text: Where grit is often seen in flying circles

definitions.text: Where grit is often seen in flying circles

parts.words: Where grit is often seen in flying circles
parts.note: grit as courage among aviators, really grains whirling through the air in a desert storm

explanation.surface: Aviation circles are where courage is shown.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert storm whips grit round and round through the air.

clue.text: None of it is good, we are told

definitions.text: None of it is good, we are told

parts.words: None of it is good, we are told
parts.note: the proverb says that having none of this is good: no tidings are good tidings

explanation.surface: A gloomy verdict on something everyone reports as bad.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'no news is good news' says an absence of reports is welcome.

clue.text: The first building to be floodlit?

definitions.text: The first building to be floodlit?

parts.words: The first building to be floodlit?
parts.note: floodlit read as lit up by, or set amid, the biblical Flood: the earliest vessel built to ride it out

explanation.surface: A trivia question about the first building illuminated by floodlights.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the vessel built by the patriarch was the first construction to sit amid the Flood.

clue.text: To become thus rich one needs the first word last

definitions.text: To become thus rich one needs the first word last

parts.words: To become thus rich one needs the first word last
parts.note: to get rich one must 'do well'; reorder the phrase so the opening word comes at the end to get the adjective

explanation.surface: Advice on getting rich: always have the final say.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to do well; the reordered phrase is the adjective for prosperous.

clue.text: Topping drinks tonight!

parts.note: lids that top things, and the night-time drinks that 'cap' an evening

explanation.surface: An excited invitation to excellent drinks this evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Caps are coverings on top, and nightcaps are drinks before bed.

clue.text: Serpentine plants ?

parts.note: plants that move like snakes, crawling along the ground or walls

explanation.surface: Snake-like vegetation, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that trail along surfaces are named for crawling like snakes.

clue.text: Certain printed matter

definitions.meaning: a photographic print made from a negative

explanation.surface: Some particular printed material.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure means convinced; and a photographic print from a negative is the opposite type of image.

clue.text: It should permit no grounds for complaint

definitions.text: It should permit no grounds for complaint

parts.words: It should permit no grounds for complaint
parts.note: grounds as coffee or tea dregs: a sieve should let none through to cause grumbling

explanation.surface: A rule that ought to leave no reason to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sieve for tea or coffee stops the grounds getting into the cup.

clue.text: Place-kicker in reverse

parts.note: to place something is to set it
a back is a defensive player who kicks the ball in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A goalkicker who places the ball while going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place-kicker' suggests a rugby goalkicker, but it splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse is a setback, a check to progress.

clue.text: Male slaves for sale?

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
items for sale at auction are offered as lots

explanation.surface: Men being sold at a slave market.
explanation.walkthrough: Helots were the serf class of ancient Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spartan serf class was a people kept in bondage.

clue.text: Women take it at its face value

definitions.text: Women take it at its face value

parts.words: Women take it at its face value
parts.note: something prized for what it does to the face, make-up

explanation.surface: Women accept something as it first appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty preparation is valued for the effect it has on the face.

clue.text: What everything has, said Alice's Duchess, apart from ethics

definitions.text: What everything has, said Alice's Duchess
definitions.meaning: in Alice in Wonderland the Duchess says 'Everything's got a moral, if only you can find it'

explanation.surface: A Wonderland character insisting everything has a lesson, except ethics.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is the Duchess's lesson in Carroll; as one, unconcerned with right and wrong.

clue.text: One secret love — terribly secret

indicators.note: terribly suggests the words are badly mangled and so rearranged

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A confession of a hidden romance kept dreadfully quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by an inner circle, hence secret.

clue.text: One of the Lord High Executioner's most, telling blows

definitions.text: One of the Lord High Executioner's most, telling blows

parts.words: One of the Lord High Executioner's most, telling blows
parts.note: the Lord High Executioner in The Mikado is Ko-Ko, whose initials are the boxing abbreviation for a decisive punch

explanation.surface: An executioner's most effective strokes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado the Lord High Executioner is Ko-Ko; KO is boxing's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive punch that floors an opponent, abbreviated KO like the character's name.

clue.text: This man was ready for a novel presentation

definitions.text: This man was ready for a novel presentation

parts.words: This man was ready for a novel presentation
parts.note: Captain Marryat's novel ... Ready: this word plus 'man' was Ready, the novel's title

explanation.surface: Someone prepared to give a new kind of talk.
explanation.walkthrough: Masterman Ready (1841) is a children's novel by Captain Frederick Marryat.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Marryat's novel, Ready, has the forename beginning with this word for a skipper.
